plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two 2D vectors emanating from a common origin, illustrating the geometric definition of endpoint error in optical flow evaluation. The vector labeled (u, v) represents the ground truth flow vector, while the vector labeled (u-hat, v-hat) represents the predicted flow vector; both share the same base point but point in slightly different directions and have different magnitudes. A red line segment connects the tips (endpoints) of the two vectors, and this segment is labeled Endpoint error, making explicit that the loss is the Euclidean distance between the endpoint of the prediction and the endpoint of the ground truth. This figure establishes endpoint error as a vector-space distance metric, clarifying why it is sensitive to both directional and magnitude errors in the predicted flow field.

interactionPlan.concept: Endpoint error in optical flow is the Euclidean distance between the predicted flow vector endpoint and the ground-truth flow vector endpoint, so it captures both magnitude and direction mistakes.
elements: common origin point where both flow vectors begin
black ground-truth flow vector arrow from the origin to endpoint (u, v)
black predicted flow vector arrow from the origin to endpoint (û, v̂)
label '(u, v)' near the ground-truth vector endpoint
label '(û, v̂)' near the predicted vector endpoint
red endpoint-error line segment connecting the two vector tips
label 'Endpoint error' next to the red segment
angular-error arc centered at the origin between the two vectors, visible only in angular-error mode
label 'Angular error' next to the angle arc, visible only in angular-error mode
numeric metric readout showing the current endpoint-error distance or angular-error value

interactions.teaches: Moving the predicted endpoint changes the error according to how far the prediction lands from the ground-truth endpoint, not just according to how different the vector angles look
Changing the reference flow vector redefines the target endpoint, so the same prediction can become more or less accurate depending on the ground truth

interactions.label: Error metric
interactions.teaches: Endpoint error measures straight-line distance between vector tips, while angular error measures only the angle between the two vectors

demo_steps.title: Endpoint error is a distance between tips
demo_steps.narration: The two flow vectors share the same origin, but their endpoints differ. The red segment is the endpoint error: the Euclidean distance from the predicted endpoint to the ground-truth endpoint.

demo_steps.title: Move the prediction
demo_steps.narration: Drag the predicted tip (û, v̂). The red segment stretches or shrinks in real time, showing that both direction and length errors change the endpoint distance.

demo_steps.title: Move the reference
demo_steps.narration: Now drag the ground-truth tip (u, v). The target endpoint moves, so the endpoint-error segment repositions even if the prediction stays fixed.

demo_steps.title: Compare with angular error
demo_steps.narration: Switch to angular error. The highlighted quantity moves from the line between endpoints to the angle at the origin, showing that angular error ignores pure magnitude differences along the same direction.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Endpoint error is not the angle between flow vectors; it is the straight-line distance between where the predicted and true vectors end.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean white background with no axes or grid, matching the textbook style. Draw both vectors as thick black arrows starting at the lower-left common origin: the ground-truth vector should be longer and steeper, ending above the predicted vector; the predicted vector should be shorter and shallower, ending down and to the right of the ground-truth tip. In endpoint-error mode, draw a thick red segment directly connecting the two arrow tips and place the 'Endpoint error' label near it. In angular-error mode, de-emphasize or hide the red segment and instead draw a colored arc centered at the origin between the two arrows. Keep the vector labels large and math-styled, with hats clearly visible on the predicted components.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Drag the estimated vector tip (û,v̂) in any direction and see the red endpoint error segment stretch or shrink in real time as the distance between the two vector tips updates
- Drag the ground-truth vector tip (u,v) to set a new reference flow direction and magnitude, watching the red error segment reposition accordingly
- Toggle between endpoint error (straight-line distance between vector tips) and angular error (angle between the two vectors) metrics, highlighting which geometric quantity each measures in the diagram

- Drag the estimated vector tip (û,v̂) in any direction and see the red endpoint error segment stretch or shrink in real time as the distance between the two vector tips updates
- Drag the ground-truth vector tip (u,v) to set a new reference flow direction and magnitude, watching the red error segment reposition accordingly

authoredContext: In supervised optical flow estimation, the most common loss is the **endpoint error**, which is the average, over the whole image, if the distance between the estimated optical flow vector, $(\hat{u},\hat{v})$ and the ground-truth vector, $(u,v)$: $$\mathcal{L} \left( \hat{\mathbf{u}}, \hat{\mathbf{v}}, \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \right) = \sum_{n,m} (\hat{u}[n,m] - u[n,m])^2 + (\hat{v}[n,m] - v[n,m])^2$$ The sum is over all the pixels in the image. Each pixel has an estimated optical flow $(\hat{u}[n,m],\hat{v}[n,m])$.

discrepancies: The generated default view includes a prominent right-side instructional/control panel and metric readout that are absent from the source static diagram, so it is not a clean drop-in replacement at a glance.
The arrow origin is inset from the lower-left edge rather than beginning exactly at the corner as in the source, changing the textbook crop/composition.
The labels are close but not exact: '(u,v)' omits the source spacing '(u, v)', and the label positions/sizes are slightly more compact than the original.
The generated figure has an extra angular-error mode that introduces a blue arc and label not present in the source figure, although it is hidden in the default state.
evaluation.notes: The core endpoint-error diagram is reproduced very well with correct vectors, red endpoint segment, and labels, but the surrounding UI and slight crop/label differences make it less like a pure static replacement.
action_items: Make the default/static composition match the source more closely by placing the vector origin at the lower-left corner and scaling the arrows to fill the available figure area similarly.
Adjust label text and placement to match the source more exactly, including '(u, v)' spacing and the larger textbook-style placement of the endpoint label.
Consider docking or minimizing the explanatory UI by default so the rendered first view reads primarily as the original diagram.
